system_overview: This specification models Safra's termination detection algorithm (EWD998) with explicit message channel modeling. Unlike the base EWD998 specification that uses counters for pending messages, this variant models channels as sequences (inboxes) containing typed messages. Both payload messages and the token are represented as messages in node inboxes, providing a more concrete model that is closer to an implementation while remaining faithful to the abstract algorithm.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, each with an inbox (message sequence). The inbox holds two types of messages: token messages (carrying a counter and color for the termination detection algorithm) and payload messages (representing computation messages). There is always exactly one token message across all inboxes. The system is divided into System (token management) and Environment (computation message sending, receiving, and node deactivation).
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) activation status of each node, (2) color of each node (white or black), (3) a counter for each node tracking messages sent minus messages received, and (4) an inbox for each node containing a sequence of typed messages (both token and payload messages).
initial_state: All per-node counters are zero. The token (a black token message with counter zero) may start in any single node's inbox. Node activation and colors may take any type-correct values.
actions: The algorithm defines the following actions: (1) Initiate probe: when a token message is in node 0's inbox and the previous round was inconclusive, node 0 consumes the token from its inbox and appends a fresh white token to node N-1's inbox, painting itself white. (2) Pass token: an inactive node with a token in its inbox consumes it and appends an updated token to the next node's inbox, adding its counter and propagating/setting the black color as needed, then paints itself white. (3) Send message: an active node increments its counter and appends a payload message to another node's inbox. (4) Receive message: a node with a payload message in its inbox consumes it, decrements its counter, paints itself black, and becomes active. (5) Deactivate: an active node becomes inactive.
safety_properties: The specification refines the base EWD998 specification through a refinement mapping that extracts the token position and counter from the inbox structure and counts pending payload messages. All safety properties of EWD998 are inherited through this refinement.
liveness_properties: Inherited from the base EWD998 specification through refinement.
model_bounds: A state constraint limits the number of payload messages per inbox to less than 3 and each node's counter to at most 3.
additional_assumptions: The type invariant ensures there is always exactly one token across all inboxes (singleton-type constraint). Messages within an inbox are unordered in the sense that any payload message can be consumed regardless of its position in the sequence. The specification requires the Utils module for helper operators.
